specTypes.math: Pure numerical computation using standard math libraries (numpy, scipy, sympy, mpmath). Verify mathematical identities, evaluate expressions, compare computed constants. NOT for: simulations requiring domain-specific packages, ML training, quantum computing, or anything needing libraries beyond standard scientific Python.
specTypes.parameter_sweep: Sweep a mathematical parameter across a range using standard math libraries. The function being swept must be expressible as pure Python math — no ML frameworks, no physics engines, no domain simulators. Good for: testing how a formula behaves across a range. NOT for: training models at different hyperparameters.
specTypes.convergence_analysis: Test whether a mathematically-defined series, sequence, or iterative formula converges. Must be expressible as a closed-form or simple recursive computation. NOT for: empirical convergence of training algorithms or simulations.
specTypes.curve_shape: Analyze the shape of a mathematically-defined function (monotonicity, extrema, inflection points, bounds). The function must be computable from a formula. NOT for: empirical curves from data or simulations.
specTypes.quantum_model: Quantum mechanical computations using density matrices, Hamiltonians, and measurement operators on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. Tests claims about entanglement, Bell inequalities, quantum state evolution, coupling regimes, non-classical states, decoherence, photon statistics. Implemented as linear algebra (numpy/scipy) on Hilbert spaces — no quantum computing packages needed.
specTypes.wave_system: Wave propagation, band structures, topological invariants, scattering and transmission analysis. Tests claims about photonic/phononic crystals, edge states, topological protection, waveguide modes, disorder robustness. Implemented via transfer matrices, tight-binding Hamiltonians, eigenvalue problems (numpy/scipy) — no FDTD or FEM solvers needed.
specTypes.coupled_dynamics: Coupled dynamical systems: optomechanical cavities, nonlinear oscillators, feedback loops, threshold and bifurcation behavior. Tests claims about strong coupling, critical thresholds, stability, parametric amplification, Langevin dynamics. Implemented via ODE/SDE integration, stability analysis, Floquet theory (scipy.integrate, scipy.linalg) — no domain-specific physics engines needed.
specTypes.many_body_model: Many-body condensed matter and quantum materials: BCS superconductivity, exciton-polaron formation, superfluid weight, quasiparticle spectral functions, Green's functions, self-energy, mean-field phase diagrams. Tests claims about Cooper pairing, gap equations, topological superconductors, proximity effects, van der Waals heterostructures. Implemented via BdG Hamiltonians, Matsubara Green's functions, self-consistent mean-field loops, and spectral function computation (numpy/scipy + numba JIT) — no QuTiP, DMFT packages, or domain-specific condensed matter codes needed.
